title: WildinSync-eDNA Sampling of Rivers
author: Loïc Pellissier
materials: Follow the specific protocol for the procedure.

steps.title: Prepare Workspace and Safety Gear
steps.instruction: Establish a dedicated filtration workspace away from DNA contamination sources. Wear nitrile gloves at all times, non-slip footwear, weather-appropriate clothing, and a personal flotation device (mandatory on vessels). Handle bleach and preservatives with gloves and safety glasses.

steps.title: Set Up Peristaltic Pump
steps.instruction: Position the Naturelink peristaltic pump on a raised, flat surface (e.g., a flat stone) to prevent water exposure. If on a boat, secure the pump with snap hooks and rope.

substeps.instruction: Connect the battery to the pump.
Remove the superior part of the peristaltic head and place it in a secured location.

steps.title: Prepare Filtration Kits
steps.instruction: Prepare one tube kit and one capsule kit. Use bleach wipes to clean scissors/penknife and the external surfaces of the plastic kit packaging.

substeps.instruction: Use the knife to open the tubing kit packaging without removing contents.
Open the capsule bag (if separate).
Remove and put on the gloves provided in the kit; do not touch skin, the pump, or other equipment after donning gloves.

steps.title: Assemble Filtration Capsule
steps.instruction: Assemble the filtration components while keeping the strainer and screwed coupling end inside the bag until needed.

substeps.instruction: Identify the top and lower ends of the capsule and ensure the caps remain at the bottom of the bag.
Screw the threaded end of the hose onto the top end of the capsule and secure well.
Position the hose inside the pump, ensuring the capsule is aligned with the pump's flow direction arrow.
Lock the head of the peristaltic pump.
Remove the capsule from the bag, keeping the drain vertical.

steps.title: Perform eDNA Filtration
steps.instruction: Initiate filtration, recording the start time, coordinates, river width, and depth on the field sheet. If sampling from a boat, maintain a speed of approximately 3 knots along a transect.

substeps.instruction: Suspend the strainer in the water, maintaining at least 10cm distance from sediments.
Ensure the capsule remains vertical (arrow pointing down) and the drain is clear.
Align the setup with the water current to prevent discharge from being re-filtered.
Set the Naturelink pump to 50% speed for 1 hour. If flow does not reduce after 10 minutes, increase speed to 70%.
Monitor for clogging; if turbid, stop filtration and record the volume filtered.
If the membrane is not fully covered by water, slowly unscrew the overpressure valve on top of the capsule until covered.
Optional: Calibrate pump by timing the filling of a 0.5/1 L container (target flow rate < 1 L·min⁻¹).

steps.title: Purge and Disassemble System
steps.instruction: Once 30 L of water have been filtered or the time has ended, purge the remaining water from the capsule.

substeps.instruction: With the pump still on, remove the strainer from the water (without touching the strainer) and allow air to pass through the hose to empty the capsule.
Switch off the pump.
Unscrew the pump head and remove the hose, ensuring the unprotected lower end of the capsule does not touch anything.

steps.title: Preserve the Sample
steps.instruction: Apply preservation buffer to the filtered sample using a clean buffer kit.

substeps.instruction: Open the buffer kit with clean scissors/penknife and put on the new gloves provided in the kit.
Remove the screw cap from the syringe tip.
Unscrew the hose from the capsule and immediately screw the syringe end onto the capsule.
Slowly unscrew the pressure valve of the capsule, keeping the capsule upright.
Slowly pour the entire contents of the syringe into the capsule, regulating inflow with the valve cap.
Secure the top of the capsule with the remaining cap.

steps.title: Secure and Store Samples
steps.instruction: Finalize the sample for transport and storage.

substeps.instruction: Vigorously shake the capsule up and down for at least 30 s to ensure buffer permeates the filter.
Apply a parafilm band around the caps for extra sealing.
Label the capsule with sticker (1), place it in a plastic (preferably numbered) bag, and store it in a box labeled with sticker (2).
Label the associated metadata with sticker (3) and record it in the field sheet.
Store the box in a dark place at room temperature, avoiding large temperature variations.

steps.title: Laboratory Storage
steps.instruction: Upon return to the lab, continue storing samples in a dark place at room temperature. Do not use a refrigerator or freezer.
